# Remediation ladder — how an audit finding gets fixed

<!-- SOURCE OF TRUTH. Every routine whose audit phase gates a prose writer loads THIS file
     and applies it IN FULL. Do not restate the ladder anywhere else — point at this file instead.
     In repos other than layer3 this file is GENERATED by layer3/scripts/sync-remediation-ladder.sh;
     edit the layer3 copy.

     Companion files, loaded by the audit phase alongside this one:
       .claude/commands/_content-standard.md     — what the gates ARE
       .claude/commands/_anti-ai-language.md     — the tell list
       .claude/commands/_experience.md           — who "we" are on this site
     This file does not define a single gate. It defines only what happens AFTER one fails. -->

<!-- fleet-audit-exhaustion-publish-v1 -->
**Fleet rule — publish when audits/reworks are exhausted (narrow direct-liability exception ONLY, 2026-11-13):** Across all Mindmap and non-Mindmap content routines on the fleet, once all allowed audits (`1` for `light`, `2` for `standard`, `2`/`3` for `high` in Mindmap; or max 2 Rung-2 reworks in non-Mindmap routines) are exhausted, **automatically publish the exact final audited version** (logging any remaining non-liability findings honestly in the run report) instead of blocking, stopping, reverting, dropping, marking `draft: true`, or asking the user how held pages should go out — and NEVER edit a Mindmap route after its final allowed audit completes. **The ONLY content exception that blocks publication at audit exhaustion is direct legal or physical-harm liability from publishing incorrect actionable information** (`liabilityBlock`: incorrect/fabricated medical dosing, prescription regimens or dangerous drug interactions/contraindications; acute physical/infant/electrical/chemical safety hazards; or defamatory illegal-conduct accusations, unlawful financial/tax directives, or fabricated clinical/lab testing or clinician sign-off — plus explicit `professionalReviewRequired: true`, explicit paid-client holds, or broken build/HTTP 404/500). **General medical/health pricing, clinic locations, addresses, hours, provider directories, scheduling/insurance logistics, general educational condition overviews, vendor comparisons, attribution wording, `scopeAndExclusions`, and SEO/style/tell findings NEVER block publication once audits are exhausted.**
<!-- /fleet-audit-exhaustion-publish-v1 -->

**Fleet editorial release.** For a Mindmap page covered by the active repository’s editorial release policy, publish the exact independently reviewed version at the first PASS or final allowed audit (LIGHT 1, STANDARD 2, HIGH 3). Retain the verdict and findings and complete the native build, deployment, links and exact live comparison. Apply this rule to the per-page stopping instructions below. Keep professional review, testing honesty and explicit client commitments.

**WHY THIS FILE EXISTS.** Audit phases used to say: on any failure, hand notes back to the writer phase and re-run; max 2 attempts, then STOP the whole run. That treated a 161-character meta description exactly like a fabricated legal claim. Measured on layer3 on 2026-09-02: writing five pages took 12 minutes and the audit-and-rework tail took 76, because each one-line fix re-entered the writer phase, reloaded the full content standard, and re-audited every page in the run including ones that had already passed. A run on 2026-09-01 was killed outright by two rounds of findings that were all one-line edits — a 161-char meta description, "three groups" listing four, an undefined acronym. Nothing shipped.

The audit itself is not the problem and does not get weaker here. On 2026-08-22 the same gates caught a fabricated vendor claim repeated in six places and two legal errors on a compliance page. **This file changes only the cost of fixing a finding, never the bar for passing one.** Every gate in `_content-standard.md` and `_anti-ai-language.md` still applies exactly as written.

---


**Humanized intro: style-only exemption.** Humanization runs before final rendered approval. Do not polish or rework a humanized intro for style. Final facts, meaning, reader intent, evidence/testing claims, links, disclosures and layout remain in scope. On a regression, restore the original intro verbatim, then recapture and review the affected page under `_rendered-page-audit.md`.

## THE LADDER

A finding is fixed at the **cheapest rung that can fix it**. Never send a one-line fix through a full writer re-run and a full re-audit of every page.

### Rung 0 — mechanical lint, before any reviewer reads a word

Run the repo's mechanical content lint on every page the writer phase produced or materially edited:

```bash
npx tsx scripts/content_lint.mts --slug <slug> [--slug <slug> …]     # TS/JS repos
python3 scripts/content_lint.py --slug <slug> [--slug <slug> …]      # markdown/frontmatter repos
```

The lint covers **only black-and-white rules**: em-dash, exclamation mark, heading not in Title Case, meta title and description length, missing required fields, an unsubstituted `{BUSINESS_NAME}`, a malformed or duplicate slug, and a dead internal link. Any FAIL → apply the fix directly (the message names the file, the field, and the offending text) and re-run until it exits 0.

Lint findings **never reach the reviewer, never count as a rework attempt, and never trigger a standard reload.** If the writer phase skipped the lint, run it here first — do not start the reviewer checklist on a page that still fails it.

**The depth gate is a Rung 0 check too.** Where the audit phase says to run `npm run check-depth`, that script measures built output. Use the following order to establish depth; source measurement alone never substitutes for final rendered review:

1. `[ -d node_modules ] || npm ci --no-audit --no-fund` (fall back to `npm install --no-audit --no-fund` if there is no lockfile), then `npm run build`, then `npm run check-depth` on the new routes. Exit 0 = pass; non-zero = the named pages are under their floor.
2. If the install or build fails, record the reason and measure source prose as a provisional depth check: concatenate each affected page’s intro, section bodies, FAQ answers and verdict, excluding title, metadata, schema, CTA boilerplate and code. Count with a real command and compare with the applicable floor. Record `depth: measured from source (build unavailable: <reason>)`. Resolve the build/runtime failure before final rendered review and publication.

Source measurement can establish the word-count floor. It cannot establish a rendered-page PASS. Final approval and publication remain blocked until the complete actual render is available and independently checked under `_rendered-page-audit.md`.

**If this repo has no lint script**, the reviewer performs the same mechanical checks itself as an explicit FIRST pass, reports them as `MECHANICAL`, and the orchestrator applies those fixes directly. Mechanical findings still never count as a rework attempt. Do not add judgment gates (neutrality, "honest", inflated adjectives, register, depth) to a lint script — those need a reader and belong to the reviewer.

### Rung 1 — FIX-IN-PLACE (reviewer supplies the replacement; no writer round-trip)

For every finding where the reviewer can quote the offending text **and** write the exact replacement, the reviewer's report carries both, in this shape:

```
FIX <page> <field>: "<offending text>" → "<replacement text>"
```

Typical Rung 1 findings: a ChatGPT tell, a pseudo-cleft, an unlinked directive (add the deep link), a coy abstraction (substitute the real name), an unlinked company first-mention (link it), a headline tell, a subtitle restatement, an orphaned first-person "we", a tee-up in the wrong position, a self-asserted neutrality sentence (delete it), a bare feature missing its consequence, a stale "last updated" date on an edited page.

The **orchestrator** applies each replacement verbatim with a targeted edit, re-runs Rung 0, then asks the reviewer to re-read **only the edited fields in their surrounding paragraph** and confirm each fix. Do not reload the content standard for this. Do not re-run the writer phase. Do not re-audit pages that were not edited. **A fix-in-place round is not a rework attempt.**

The rule the reviewer follows: if you can write the corrected sentence, you have already done the work — hand over the replacement rather than a complaint. A finding reported without a replacement, where one was possible, is an incomplete report.

**Unsupported claims are Rung 1 too (API-written pages).** An invented, unsourced, contradicted or inferred claim — a sentence, bullet or table cell the closed fact list does not support — is fixed IN PLACE by deleting it or restating what the fact list does say. Never by regenerating the page: a whole-page re-roll rewrites every sentence and fails on NEW invented claims (2026-10: 19 of 19 drafts dropped that way across 8 routines). For a page written by `scripts/lib/content_gen.py`, save the reviewer's findings for that page (quote + defect per finding, claims AND tells) to a file and run:

```bash
python3 scripts/lib/content_gen.py fix --draft <draft> --findings <findings.txt> \
    --facts <row prompt> --floor <floor> [--allowed-urls <urls.txt>]
```

It splices model-written replacements by exact string match (a replacement may only restate the fact list, or delete), runs one claim-check pass that deletes anything the replacements left unsupported, keeps a `.pre-fix-N` backup, and lists anything it could not fix as `NOT FIXABLE IN PLACE`. Then apply the draft to the store, re-run Rung 0, and re-audit **the fixed page in full** (the bar is unchanged: zero unsupported claims). `fix` never adds a fact and is not a rework attempt, **and neither is a re-audit that still finds claims or tells after a fix round**: save those new findings to a fresh findings file and run `fix` again, up to **3 fix rounds per page** (pages near the fact-budget edge routinely need 2). A failed post-`fix` re-audit never counts toward the Rung 2 cap and never drops a page by itself (2026-10-08 keyword-gap: both drafts were dropped as "failed the audit twice" after one fix round, while same-day mindmap pages with thinner fact lists shipped after their second). Only what `fix` lists as NOT FIXABLE IN PLACE, a page its fixes push under the depth floor, an auditor note that the floor can only be met by restating facts, or a page still failing after 3 fix rounds goes to Rung 2.

### Rung 2 — REWORK (back to the writer, this page only)

Reserved for findings that need new substance, new research, or a structurally different page:

- a claim `content_gen.py fix` reported NOT FIXABLE IN PLACE (the page needs a fact it does not have)
- depth under the floor after unsupported claims were removed, or a page that can only reach its floor by restating the same facts: EXPAND THE CLOSED FACT LIST with sourced facts first (the draft meta's `thin fact list` flag says so), then regenerate; never pad, never loosen the audit
- an experience claim `_experience.md` does not license
- the wrong register for what the page does
- depth under the floor for its page type
- a missing required page element (direct answer up top, who-this-is-not-for, what-would-change-our-answer, the proprietary anchor)
- a dead-end problem the page raises and never resolves
- a section that has to be rewritten rather than repaired

Hand the reviewer's notes for **that page only** to the writer phase and re-run it for that page. A regenerated API page gets the claim check again automatically; anything the audit still finds goes back through Rung 1 `fix`, not straight to another rework. The reworked page then gets a full audit again, from Rung 0.

**One shared Mindmap audit budget & fleet auto-publish at exhaustion.** An activated Mindmap page has its configured total 1/2/3 independent rounds, including corrections; there is no separate two-rework allowance. Once all allowed audits (or max 2 Rung-2 reworks in non-Mindmap routines) are exhausted, stop editorial edits immediately and automatically publish the exact final audited candidate with FAIL findings logged honestly — blocking ONLY for narrow direct legal/physical-harm liability edge cases (`liabilityBlock`, e.g. incorrect medical dosing or acute safety hazards; never general medical pricing, clinic locations, scheduling, educational overviews, attribution phrasing, or SEO/style notes), explicit `professionalReviewRequired: true`, explicit client holds, or broken build/HTTP 404/500. Preserve unrelated work and unchanged-page evidence.

---

## PER-PAGE PASS STATE

A page that PASSED stays passed. Fixing or reworking one page does not re-open the audit on its siblings, and the rework counter is **per page**, never per phase. This is what stops one bad page from consuming both attempts on behalf of a batch that was otherwise fine.

This does not weaken the re-audit invariant: a page whose own text changed is always re-checked on that exact text (Rung 1 re-reads the edited fields in context; Rung 2 re-audits the page in full). What is forbidden is re-auditing a page whose bytes did not change.

The reviewer report ends with one line per page:

```
<page>: PASS | FIX-IN-PLACE (n) | REWORK (attempt k/2) | PUBLISH-AT-AUDIT-LIMIT | BLOCKED-LIABILITY — <direct legal/physical harm>
```

## Actual dependency & direct-liability failures

A required mechanical build/runtime/HTTP-200 check, canonical instruction check, independent-review execution, explicit `professionalReviewRequired: true`, explicit paid-client hold, or narrow direct legal/physical-harm `liabilityBlock` (e.g. incorrect medical dosing — never general medical pricing, locations, attribution wording, `scopeAndExclusions`, or SEO/style findings) remains enforced. Repair mechanical issues automatically within existing authority, retaining exact work and evidence; report an actual unavailable dependency or `liabilityBlock` honestly while publishing all non-blocked sibling pages. Once audits/reworks are exhausted without a `liabilityBlock`, automatically publish the exact final audited candidate — never fabricate a PASS, edit post-cap, or silently add another audit.
**Owner fleet audit-exhaustion auto-publish & narrow legal-liability exception, November 13, 2026.** Across the entire fleet, once all allowed independent audits are exhausted (`1` for `light`, `2` for `standard`, `2` or `3` for `high`), **automatically publish the exact final audited snapshot** (`disposition: "publish-at-audit-limit"`). NEVER block, hold, revert, mark `draft: true`, drop, or ask the user how held pages should go out, and NEVER edit or rebuild a route after its final allowed audit round completes (post-cap edits invalidate the final audited snapshot while `reserve` refuses another round). **The ONLY content exception (`liabilityBlock`) is tip-top edge cases creating direct legal or physical-harm liability from publishing incorrect actionable information**, recorded on a `FAIL` route as `"liabilityBlock": {"category": "<medical-dosing-or-treatment-harm|acute-physical-safety-hazard|unlawful-or-defamatory-liability>", "quote": "<exact >=8-char page substring>", "harm": "<>=40-char direct legal/physical harm explanation>"}` (plus explicit `professionalReviewRequired: true` or explicit paid-client prepublication hold): (1) `medical-dosing-or-treatment-harm` (incorrect/fabricated medication dosing, prescription regimens, dangerous drug interactions/contraindications, pediatric/pregnancy dosing, emergency triage directives, or unverified clinical cure/treatment directives that could injure a # Claim-based review depth and one per-page audit budget

Owner instruction, 2026-11-08. Applies to Mindmap Pass and routines that hand content to it across the fleet. This contract supersedes older uniform factual depth, separate fix-round allowances and separate two-rework limits for ordinary editorial content. It does not change Phase 0 authorization, independent preparation/chart review, publication scope, full SEO, source/testing honesty, site exclusions, professional obligations or native paid-client/upsell release policies. A capped release retains factual FAIL findings; it never converts them to verified facts or an editorial PASS.

## Depth follows actual claims

The site's `.claude/content-review-policy.json` supplies its default and floor. LIGHT has at most ONE independent content-review round; STANDARD at most TWO; HIGH at most TWO unless the independent review establishes a genuine medical or legal claim. Bot Scout always has at most TWO. These are ceilings, never targets: publish after the first genuine PASS once all normal release checks succeed.

- LIGHT: ordinary grooming, reading and product-use guides. Check central facts, truthful evidence/testing language and the reader's answer. Do not perform clinical/legal investigations on content that makes no such claims.
- STANDARD: general AI/software/product comparisons. Also verify material prices, availability, capabilities, important numbers and recommendation conditions from appropriate sources.
- HIGH: medical/treatment, consequential legal/financial/investment/security/safety claims and stricter site floors. Add current primary sources, conditions/units/jurisdictions, contrary evidence and any genuinely required professional review. Three AI rounds never substitute for required professional review.

Every level keeps the complete applicable SEO/intent/demand/deduplication, usefulness, attribution, testing-label, indexability, link, schema/date, rendered-layout and exact-live checks. Preserve specific local owner exemptions, including American Pivot's existing no-keyword/demand-gate scope. A health or safety claim on a nominally low-risk site escalates. A risk word occurring only in a related URL is not itself a consequential claim. Incidental visible mentions need exact-passage explanations, independently checked; missing/uncertain classification stays HIGH. Review all actual reader claims, including inherited text and descriptive metadata/schema. Do not hide a risky paragraph or reclassify genuine advice as incidental to obtain a cheaper profile.

## One actual counter, including corrections

The initial independent content audit is round 1. Every subsequent independent AI verification counts too, whether called `fix-in-place`, claim check, final QA, rework or re-audit. The three old fix rounds and two old rework attempts do NOT create extra allowances. Deterministic lint/build/link/hash checks and the separate preparation/chart review do not consume editorial rounds and cannot make an editorial PASS. A writer's internal validation does not replace the independent audit or create an additional independent-review budget.

Track each canonical site/page in the append-only journal managed by `.claude/tools/content-review-policy.py`. Retain actual source-bound reports, findings, attempts and canonical job across retries/conversations; a different run ID or draft filename cannot reset the counter. Import actual pre-existing content-review reports in their real order on resumption. Never count a chart review as a content review, manufacture missing reports, omit prior failed reviews or convert a failure into PASS.

After the limit, stop editorial work on that page and automatically publish the exact latest reviewed candidate where releaseAtAuditLimit is enabled, unless the route carries a validated `liabilityBlock` (`medical-dosing-or-treatment-harm`, `acute-physical-safety-hazard`, or `unlawful-or-defamatory-liability`) or explicit `professionalReviewRequired: true`. All non-liability FAIL findings — including general medical pricing, clinic locations, scheduling/insurance details, educational condition summaries, attribution phrasing (`testingAndAttribution`), `scopeAndExclusions`, and SEO/style findings — publish automatically at audit exhaustion: preserve them honestly, preserve all counters, never edit the exhausted route again, and use the normal default-branch deployment and exact live checks. Do not hold an ordinary or general-medical page, omit it from a mixed batch, restart writing, ask the user how held pages should go out, or request another audit because of those findings. Native client/upsell workflows retain their own release rules. No additional human gate is created.

## Existing Phase 4 integration

1. Mark the normal render manifest with `workflowKind: "mindmap-pass"` before capture. Use the existing production-path full capture after all content/template/link changes. Capture attaches the active policy hash; it is not approval.
2. The independent auditor uses `content-review-policy.py classify --snapshot SNAPSHOT --route ROUTE` to see the site's provisional profile, actual risk passages and text hash. The reviewer writes a genuine `riskAssessment` with `textSha256`, a specific `rationale`, `consequentialClaims` (exact quote, category and reason) and `incidentalMentions` (exact contextual quote and reason). HIGH needs no repetitive explanation of every medical keyword; lower classifications must account for all flagged passages. Quotes/reasons must describe the actual page, not copied fixture answers.
3. BEFORE the independent content audit, reserve its actual round:

   `python3 .claude/tools/content-review-policy.py reserve --snapshot SNAPSHOT --route ROUTE --job-id ORIGINAL_JOB --reviewer ACTUAL_AUDITOR --out NEW_ADMISSION.json`

   For a legacy unfinished job, repeat `--prior-review ACTUAL_OLD_REPORT.json` for every real previous content round. An already pending identical reservation is resumed; it is not permission to audit a changed draft without another slot. The first independent judgment can resolve a conservative provisional risk classification; later rounds cannot lower the established risk or erase history.
4. The real rendered review keeps all existing seven checks, author/reviewer independence and exact fingerprints. Each route additionally carries `reviewProfile`, its actual independent `riskAssessment`, `reviewBudget: {path, sha256}` referencing the reservation, and evidence-backed `factualReview` fields. LIGHT requires `centralFacts`, `truthfulEvidence`; STANDARD adds `currentDetails`, `recommendationSupport`; HIGH adds `primarySources`, `consequentialClaims`, `limitationsAndJurisdiction`, `professionalReview`. All levels add `riskClassification` and `seoQuality`; sites already requiring `instructionUnderstanding` retain it. Use real observations, not generated PASS defaults. An inapplicable professional check needs a specific NA reason; a required one needs its real artifact.
5. Record the actual per-route PASS/FAIL before applying another correction:

   `python3 .claude/tools/content-review-policy.py record --review ACTUAL_RENDERED_REVIEW.json`

   This records the review; it never generates a verdict. A changed candidate uses the next reservation under the SAME job and page journal. Keep the same independent reviewer where its genuine current context can be retained. Follow normal complete-reading, access/understanding and context-loss requirements.
6. Run the existing rendered check and Mindmap analysis audit. Their policy hooks require the actual recorded PASS or the exact final capped FAIL release within budget. Publishing uses that exact independently reviewed content and existing build/link/live/host checks. `rendered-audit.py record-deployment` closes the cycle only after verified publication; land the appended journal and its immutable admissions/reports with the normal internal receipts. A future genuinely new revision may then begin a new cycle. A failed/unpublished page cannot acquire a new budget by changing its job ID.

If a multi-page review leaves a page held but others genuinely passed, retain those exact approvals with `python3 .claude/tools/content-review-policy.py project --snapshot SNAPSHOT --review ACTUAL_REVIEW --route PASSING_ROUTE --out-snapshot SUBSET_SNAPSHOT --out-review SUBSET_REVIEW` (repeat `--route` as needed). This is a mechanical subset of the same evidence, not a new audit or verdict. It can include an actual recorded PASS or an authorized exact final capped FAIL, with all findings unchanged. Do not use a subset to omit a release-eligible capped page. Keep the original snapshot/review unchanged. Use `sources --review ACTUAL_REVIEW` to list the exact internal journal, admissions and frozen report dependencies to retain with normal publication receipts; retain the appended journal again after verified live closure. None belongs in visitor-facing files.

Existing source-bound snapshot/review pairs enumerated before activation still run their ORIGINAL validators; the inventory is not a new PASS or a retrospective understanding attestation. New candidates must use this policy. Preserve any native client/upsell exception solely through its existing validating release path, with actual counters, eligibility and holds intact; an ordinary editorial caller cannot self-declare such an exception.

## Release-gate integration (authority snapshots, compositions, record-time proof)

- **Authority, not wrapper.** A projection or composition is only a wrapper. Risk text, profile, reviewer and the recorded report digest are verified against the ORIGINAL independent snapshot/report that judged each page. Never verify against a re-saved copy: canonical saving sorts JSON keys and changes the passage order the reviewer hashed.
- **Separately recorded passes.** When different pages passed in different recorded reports (for example one page in a later round and its unchanged siblings earlier), join them for one publication snapshot with `content-review-policy.py compose --snapshot FINAL_SNAPSHOT --spec SPEC.json --out-review COMPOSITE_REVIEW.json`. `SPEC.json` lists `groups` (`snapshot`, `review`, `routes`) and, on Layer3, `bindings` (`policyCommit`, `workflowPolicySha256`, `writer` and `reviewer` bundle `manifest.json`). Each route must carry its exact recorded PASS or authorized final capped FAIL row, an identical fingerprint, semantic content, text hash and manifest entry in the final snapshot, one author and one independent reviewer, and its own latest eligible journal verdict. It writes no verdict, changes no recorded digest and fails closed on anything missing, forged or edited after review. `sources --review COMPOSITE_REVIEW.json` lists every file to retain, including the bound bundles.
- **Layer3 instruction proof.** A recorded PASS must be releasable. `record` therefore requires, BEFORE spending the round, either the existing current `workflowPolicySha256` + `instructionApplications`, or `releaseBindings` (`policyCommit`, `workflowPolicySha256`, `writer`, `reviewer`) that the immutable-delivery verifier accepts: the actual author and reviewer actors and roles, one invocation, the canonical job's handoff, the policy recomputed at the named commit, and every bundle source equal to that commit. `record` validates every page of a report before appending any, so a later failing page cannot leave a partly recorded report.
- **Earlier policy hashes.** Editing the policy tool changes its own hash. `compatiblePolicies` in `.claude/content-review-policy.json` lists exact earlier hashes whose already-admitted and recorded reviews stay valid; new reservations always need the current hash.
- **Admission.** `audit-admission.local.py` and `fresh-preview.local.py` refuse a candidate whose manifest lacks `workflowKind` or, for `mindmap-pass`, whose capture is not stamped with the active policy, before any reviewer is assigned. A native client/upsell path names its own explicit `workflowKind`.

Owner durable-review continuation 2026-11-09: Install content-review-durable.py with content-review-policy.py and workflow-control-store.py (and their regression tests). reserve/record automatically retain the actual hash-chained journal, admissions, rendered/source artifacts and original PASS/FAIL reports in the native non-forced Git control store. A clean checkout restores that exact history before another reservation. A genuine partial result remains recorded when a later route is invalid; native all-or-nothing validation stays all-or-nothing. Missing/conflicting evidence blocks, never resets a counter or invents a PASS. Exact passing-subset projection preserves the original source assessment and independent evidence; a serializer repair is not a new editorial audit. Existing native composition and stricter rules remain.

## Immutable captures and incomplete review records

Use a fresh run-owned loopback preview process from the current build for a changed candidate; retire only this run's old process. Never capture a new revision from a still-running old `next start`. Every capture output and its HTML/text folder is immutable: use a new versioned output path. The durable backend archives the exact earlier dependency bytes by hash while keeping the writer's current files intact. A prior artifact resolves only to bytes matching its original hash, never the newly edited file.

A reserved slot is pending, not a completed audit, and cannot release a changed page. If a pending snapshot was overwritten, retain the actual auditor failure handback and the lost snapshot hash. Use `content-review-policy.py repair-pending --snapshot ACTUAL_CORRECT_CAPTURE --route ORIGINAL_ROUTE --job-id ORIGINAL_JOB --reviewer ACTUAL_INDEPENDENT_REVIEWER --out NEW_ADMISSION --failure ACTUAL_FAILURE_HANDOFF`. This performs one append-only mechanical rebind of that same unfinished numbered slot, preserves all original events, findings and counters, and grants no verdict or extra round. It rejects intact or completed admissions and a second repair of the same slot. Complete the real independent result with normal `record`; reuse the actual original auditor when its context remains available. No new writing, chart, generation or completed-page audit is authorized by this metadata repair. An old ledger-done flag cannot hide a pending audit. Preserve genuine required professional approval, exclusions, testing honesty and native client/upsell rules. No additional human gate.

For Node/Next/Astro audit previews, use `python3 .claude/tools/preview-session.py start --run-id ACTUAL_INVOCATION_RUN_ID --route ACTUAL_ROUTE` after the normal build. It reuses only this invocation's verified unchanged build, otherwise starts a fresh owned loopback process and retires its old process. Capture uses its returned baseUrl and verifies the build and current source signature before fetching pages. The helper does not perform an audit or generate content. `stop --run-id ACTUAL_INVOCATION_RUN_ID` retires only the matching owned process. Python/native preview adapters retain their existing paths. To restore hash-bound earlier dependency bytes before a pending repair, use `content-review-durable.py restore --canonical-base ACTUAL_ORIGIN --route ACTUAL_ROUTE`; it preserves the writer's current files and creates no review verdict.

Before the first content-audit reservation, MAIN seals the writer’s actual current canonical handoff through workflow-handoff.py; it must not delegate an auditor without that handoff. The actual independent auditor completes AUDIT preflight with its real actor/run/context/epoch and passes `--preflight ITS_COMPLETED_DIRECTORY` to `content-review-policy.py reserve`. A BUILD receipt or directly reading some contracts is not an AUDIT checkpoint. Missing handoff/reading is repaired before substantive audit, without reserving a slot, restarting research or dropping same-context instruction reuse. The guard does not invalidate or repeat genuine completed historical content verdicts: preserve any historical procedural failure honestly and apply the corrected checkpoint to the next actual stage.

For an existing pending audit reservation with a corrupted source dependency, use the existing repair-pending command on the same job and round with its retained failure evidence and a replacement snapshot. The validator compares source hashes and retains the original and replacement identities. The independent reviewer must complete that slot. A recorded verdict cannot use this repair.

**For `article` format rows — and for `comparison table/database` rows that Phase 3 generated as REAL pages (a `<slug>.meta.json` exists):** apply the standard checklist below. **API-generated pages (the normal case — see `_content-generation.md`):** hand the auditor the run's **closed fact list(s)** (`reports/mindmap-pass/<TODAY>/prompts/<slug>.prompt.md`) and **`allowed-urls.txt`** alongside the drafts, plus each draft's `meta.guards`. An auditor working from a trimmed fact set will flag TRUE sourced facts as fabrication. Before acting on any "unsupported claim" finding, verify it against the source; keep confirmed facts, cut only what no source supports. Findings are actionable only with the exact quoted text; fixes follow the remediation ladder (mechanical in place first).

---

<!-- CRON_PROMPT_START -->
<!-- mindmap-visible-checks-cron-v1 -->
Show the approval chart only after all applicable preparation passes independent chart review under `_workflow-checkpoints.md`. Show one aggregate Preparation check row: Passed with linked evidence, or Failed with only the specific failures and approval blocked; keep the full checklist in the linked report. Every new-page action requires its complete, matching actual per-page brief inline in BOTH saved and displayed approval charts under `_workflow-checkpoints.md`; missing briefs block presentation. Writing, content audit, internal-link changes and publication stay in the future execution plan until approved; never pre-certify their results.

<!-- workflow-checkpoint-cron-v1 -->
**Required before executing this content phase:** Follow `.claude/commands/_workflow-checkpoints.md` in the active repository. Complete the phase-specific `workflow-preflight.py` chunk delivery and freshness check. Existing independent chart/Phase 4 audits must record rule-by-rule artifact evidence for local exclusions, provenance, visible attribution, intent takeaways, testing labels and applicable growth/visual checks. Follow `_rendered-page-audit.md`: finish central research before preparation Passed; independently audit the complete rendered decision path after template/affiliate/link changes; verify the exact reviewed render live using `rendered-audit.py` and close deployment/measurement records. A read-only reviewer may write internal receipts. A loader receipt or worker assertion is not a review PASS. Preserve the sole Phase 0 human gate.
<!-- /workflow-checkpoint-cron-v1 -->

Make sure all article pages meet metadata length requirements (title/description), follow FAQ JSON, schema.org, and have good internal linking.

**FAIL — heading not in Title Case.** Every H1 and section heading (H2/H3) must use Title Case: the first letter of each major word is capitalized. If any heading has a major word starting lowercase — e.g. `"Who Spark fits, and who should look elsewhere"`, `"Spark pros and cons"` — set fail with note `heading-case: [the heading]`. The fix is a one-field capitalization (capitalize the major words; keep minor words a/an/the/and/or/nor/but/for/to/of/in/on/at/by/with/from/vs/via/per lowercase unless first or last; preserve acronyms and brand casing like AI, API, SEO, GPT-5, iOS exactly — never lowercase them). FAQ `question` fields are exempt (they are questions, keep sentence casing).

**FAIL — byline/date in body prose.** Reviewer byline + review date belong in the header/byline area + JSON-LD schema, never in body content. If any prose field (intro, sections, verdict, callouts, FAQ answers) contains a reviewer/author attribution or review-date sentence — e.g. "Reviewed by …", "Last updated …", "on [date]", "We research using …", "[Name], Founder of …" — set fail with note "byline-in-body: [field/heading]". Fix: delete it from prose and rely on the record's date fields + the template/schema byline.

---

## Advisory notes (record, do NOT block publication)

These are NON-BLOCKING observations the reviewer records for the run summary. Do NOT set fail for any of them. The reviewer continues to auto-continue exactly as today.

- **Low Information Gain** — if a section reads like conventional wisdom with no original example, case-specific insight, or non-obvious implication, note: "low information gain: [section heading]".
- **AEO gap** — if a major section's opening sentence is a rhetorical question or transition phrase ("In this section…") rather than a self-contained declarative claim, note: "AEO: [section heading] does not open with a direct claim".
- **Missed long-tail opportunity** (NOT a quota) — only if the page targeted broad head terms while ignoring a clearly relevant question-format query that had no stronger alternative and would have fit naturally, note: "missed long-tail: [topic]". Do NOT note this merely because a page lacks question-format headings/FAQs — a page already well-targeted to stronger keywords is correct as-is.
- **Authorship missing** — if a YMYL page (compliance, finance, medical, legal) has Organization-only author, no Person JSON-LD, or no `reviewer`/`lastReviewed` in schema, note: "authorship: [missing element]". (The visible byline belongs in the header + schema — do NOT expect or reward a "reviewed by" line in body prose; that is a FAIL, see above.)
- **Missing external link** — if the page names a clickable external entity that this project does NOT auto-link (a niche/newer tool, a specific company, a named law/standard, a cited study/dataset, or the source behind a statistic) without a link to its official primary source on first mention, note: "external link: [entity/source]". Do NOT flag entities the project auto-links at render time (common models/IDEs/AI-labs/benchmarks) — those stay plain text in the source.
- **Not task-complete** — if the page redirects out (or thin-wraps an external link) without first answering the reader's intent on-page, or cites an aggregator instead of the first-party source, note: "task-complete: [issue]".

A page with any/all of these notes and no hard-fail issues still passes audit.

---

---

## ‼️ SELF-SERVING DISCLAIMER GATE — blocks the phase (MANDATORY — added 2026-08-21)

**Never write a sentence asserting our own neutrality, independence, or lack of a financial interest.** This is a hard fail, not a style note. Strip every instance before the page ships.

Banned constructions (non-exhaustive — judge by intent, not exact wording):
- "Layer3 Labs does not resell / resells none of / does not refer / does not partner with…"
- "We take no referral fee / no commission / no kickback from…"
- "This ranking is independent." / "A note on objectivity:" / "Layer3 Labs is vendor-neutral."
- "No paid placement" / "No sponsored placement" / "We don't take payment to be listed" / "Our rankings are editorial, not paid" — the site sells paid placements, so any claim it doesn't is false.
- "We run our own repositories on this stack, so this is written from the position of someone who has to live with the choice."
- Any variant that asks the reader to trust our motives rather than showing our reasoning.

**Why this is a hard fail, on two independent grounds:**

1. **It is frequently FALSE.** This repo auto-inserts `rel="sponsored"` affiliate links via the `ENTITY_LINKS` registry in `src/utils/sectionContent.tsx`. Any entity there with `sponsored: true` (Cursor, ElevenLabs, Murf, Apollo.io, Instantly.ai, Dext, Nutshell, Pinecone, Netlify, RunPod, Carepatron, Prezi, ZoomInfo — re-read the registry, it grows) earns us a referral fee **on that very page**. A page that autolinks Cursor and also says "we take no referral fee from Cursor" is publishing a false statement about a material financial relationship. On 2026-08-21 two such sentences shipped and had to be removed.
2. **It does not work even when true.** Objectivity is demonstrated by the analysis: naming who should NOT pick our preferred option, stating what would change the verdict, and citing what each vendor actually publishes. Asserting neutrality adds nothing a skeptical reader will credit, and reads as protesting too much.

**Auditor procedure — run this on every page in the phase:**
```bash
grep -inE "does not resell|do not resell|resells? none|takes? no (referral|commission|kickback)|no commission on|does not (refer|partner)|vendor.neutral|this (ranking|comparison|page) is independent|note on objectivity|we are not (paid|sponsored)|no financial (interest|stake)|no sponsored placement|not paid placements|(do not|don.t) (charge|take payment) to be (listed|included|ranked)" <the new/edited entries>
```
Any hit → **FAIL the page** and require removal. Delete the claim outright; do not soften it. Where the sentence also carried real methodology ("we weighed what each vendor publishes about X"), keep only the methodology half and drop the financial/neutrality assertion.

**What to do instead:** nothing. Say what the page found and why. If a genuine affiliate relationship exists, that is handled by the site's affiliate-disclosure mechanism, **not** by prose in the body — and never by a sentence claiming the relationship does not exist.

**Scope note:** this gate covers the pages THIS pass creates or edits. If the auditor notices the pattern on pre-existing pages, record it as an advisory finding for the human, do not mass-edit other pages inside this run.

---

## ‼️ DEPTH GATE — deterministic, blocks the phase (MANDATORY — added 2026-08-11, ported from `/new-site`)

**This is not a reviewer judgment call and no subagent opinion overrides it.** Run it as the FIRST action of this phase and again as the last. It applies to `article` format rows only — spec-only (non-article) rows are exempt, since their deliverable is a spec, not prose.

**Measurement — use the first rung that applies:**
1. **If Phase 0 found a `check-depth` script in this repo** (`npm run check-depth`, installed by `/new-site`): run it. A non-zero exit **blocks this phase**. This is authoritative — it measures the built output, so it catches thinness the source view can miss.
2. **Otherwise, measure from source.** For each new page record, concatenate every reader-facing prose field (intro + section bodies + FAQ answers + verdict) — excluding title, meta description, schema, `inlineCta`, CTA boilerplate, and code blocks — and word-count it. Do this with an actual command (e.g. pipe the extracted text through `wc -w`), never by eyeballing length.

**Verdict:** compare each page against the floors table in `phase-3-new-content.md` (comparison/review 1,500 · persona 1,400 · hub/worth-it/explainer 1,200 · cost 1,000 · editorial 600; **explainer 1,200 is the default** for anything that doesn't clearly match another type). Any page under its floor is a **HARD FAIL** — hand it back to Phase 3 for expansion with real substance, and re-measure. It is not fixable by padding: a page that clears the floor but trips BAR 1 (AI filler) fails anyway, so expansion must add actual information.

**Report the distribution, not per-page verdicts.** Print `passing / failing / median` across all article pages this run. Page-by-page review is structurally blind to run-wide thinness — a 300-word page reads as concise and on-intent in isolation, and only the distribution shows that every page is one. On runs of 3+ article pages, a median sitting within 10% of the floor is itself a finding: record it as `depth: median {N} barely clears floor {F}` in the summary even when every page individually passes.

---

**Hand the auditor the row's `reader_question`, `answer` and `answer_placement` (chart cols 10–12) with every page.** `_content-standard.md`'s `GATE — Reader question` is audited against them — without them the auditor has to guess what the page was supposed to answer, which is how a definitional opener passed three audit rounds on 2026-09-22. Include the evidence tag (`[PAA n/m …]` / `[verb-only …]`): a verb-only question is a weaker premise and the auditor should say so rather than fail the page for missing evidence it never had.

**Remediation:** Use `_remediation-ladder.md` for mechanical and targeted correction methods, and `_content-review-policy.md` for the single total 1/2/3 independent-audit budget and release decision. These are not additional rework allowances. Keep actual PASS/FAIL judgments and reuse unchanged pages. At an activated Mindmap audit limit publish the exact final candidate with factual and cosmetic FAIL findings retained; do not stop, isolate it for editorial failure, regenerate, or buy another audit. Preserve existing non-editorial safeguards and the separate native client/upsell contracts.
<!-- CRON_PROMPT_END -->

---
## ▶ WHEN THIS PHASE IS DONE — AUTO-CONTINUE. DO NOT ASK THE USER.
The moment this phase's reviewer gate PASSES, immediately begin the next phase in the SAME turn. Do NOT stop. Do NOT print "Want me to proceed?", "Should I continue?", "Next: Phase X", or any question or hand-off that waits for a human reply.

The `/mindmap-pass` run has EXACTLY ONE human stop (the Phase 0 manifest approval), and this phase is NOT it:
- Stop 1: the Phase 0 manifest approval (before any edits).
- (Phase 8 is an informational summary that auto-continues to the Phase 9 push — NOT a stop.)

Everything between those two — including this phase — runs automatically. The reviewer gates are adversarial SUBAGENTS, not human checkpoints; a passing gate means YOU proceed on your own. Keep going through Phase 8 and the Phase 9 push without stopping.


## Updated-page date-bump rule (MANDATORY — workflow-wide, added 2026-07-12)

**Editors (any step that changes what an EXISTING page renders — metadata/title, body or enrich sections, FAQs, internal links, embedded tools, thin-content rework, link fixes):** every existing page you update MUST have its "last updated" date bumped to the run date **in the SAME change** — the content edit and the date bump ship together, never separately. Discover how THIS project surfaces the date (record it as a Phase 0 project fact) and bump the field the template ACTUALLY renders:
- **DB-backed pages** (e.g. ban_the_bots: `landing_pages.last_generated_at` renders both the visible "Last updated" byline and JSON-LD `dateModified`; `blog_posts.updated_at` for posts): any script/SQL that edits content columns MUST also set the date column to now (e.g. `page.last_generated_at = datetime.utcnow()`). Never ship an enrichment/edit script that touches content but not the date column.
- **File-backed pages**: bump the frontmatter/date field the template renders (`last_updated`, `updated`, `dateModified`, …) and re-render if the project pre-renders static HTML.

Also refresh every surface derived from that date: JSON-LD `dateModified`, and the sitemap `<lastmod>` when the generator does not derive it from the same field. **New pages created this run are exempt** (their date fields already default to now). **Purely non-rendering technical fixes are exempt** (robots.txt, redirects, canonical tags, sitemap-only hygiene) — do NOT bump dates for those.

**Auditors / reviewer gates (adversarial review):** for EVERY existing page this run edited, verify the rendered "Last updated" date (and JSON-LD `dateModified`) now equals the run date. A stale date on an updated page is a **HARD FAIL** — the page does not pass until the date is bumped. The fix is a one-field update; never rewrite the page. Conversely, a bumped date on a page whose rendered content did NOT change is also a fail (date churn fakes freshness) — revert it.

## Content standard — audit gates

**Load `.claude/commands/_content-standard.md` and apply its `## AUDITOR` section in full.** It is the single source of truth for the content gates: register and voice, tee-up, experience truth, required page elements, byline-in-body, the proprietary anchor, neutrality, disclaimer placement, depth floors, first-mention links, and the row records.

**Also load `.claude/commands/_experience.md`** — every first-person experience claim on a page must be traceable to it; anything it does not license is an invented claim and fails.

**Also load `.claude/commands/_anti-ai-language.md`** and apply its **AUDITOR** section in full, including the meaning bar. It outranks the content standard on any conflict.

If any of those files is missing, FAIL the run and report it — never substitute your own gates. If `.claude/commands/_content-standard.local.md` exists in this repo, its sections override the same-named sections of the standard.

<!-- mindmap-execution-v1 -->
Apply `_mindmap-execution.md` inside this existing audit: independently judge usefulness and source/assumption limits, replay deterministic calculations where relevant, inspect real run records for measured work, and bind the analysis decision to the exact final rendered snapshot/review. Accept justified non-quantitative and no-addition branches; do not require new paid/physical testing merely to repeat a saved valid record.
<!-- /mindmap-execution-v1 -->
